# Draft:Westward Industries

----
Westward Industries Ltd. D.B.A Westward Vehicles, located in Winnipeg Manitoba, was founded in the early 1990s to create specialized fleet utility vehicles.
The company is most well known for the GO-4 Interceptor, a compact vehicle most commonly used by police departments and public works departments for large cities as a parking enforcement vehicle.
They are also the manufacture of the Max-EV, a low-speed vehicle (LSV) built as a four-wheel heavy duty electric powered alternative.
Early History of the GO-4 Interceptor
The original design of Westward's first major vehicle, the GO-4 Interceptor, was built under contract specifications as defined by the New York Police Department (NYPD).
The vehicle was to be narrow enough to pass between rows of traffic in congested streets, while also providing more protection than what a traditional police motorcycle would.
The early designs of the GO-4 Interceptor contained a large steel frame / roll bars capable of protecting operators in the event of a collision or roll-over, but utilized a three-wheel design to allow for a very tight turning radius, further allowing the vehicle operator to navigate efficiently through busy street traffic.
Westward Industries was awarded the manufacturing contract by the NYPD for the GO-4 Interceptor which thereafter became a common sight along the streets of New York, and many cities across America to follow.
During this time several major improvements were made to the vehicle, which were introduced in additional models of the GO-4 Interceptor, the GO-4 Interceptor II, GO-4 Interceptor III, the GO-4 EV, and eventually the GO-4 Interceptor IV which was the standard model up until 2025 when Westward began production of the GO-4 Interceptor V.
Parking Specific Vehicles
After it's successful introduction as a fleet utility vehicle, the GO-4 Interceptor was beginning to be associated heavily as a "meter maid" vehicle, used predominantly by parking enforcement officers to quickly travel alongside parked vehicles without causing as much impedance on the flow of normal street traffic.
Leaning into this trend Westward Industries started manufacturing the GO-4 Interceptor with factory installed automatic license plate recognition (ALPR) systems.
This new software would allow parking enforcement officers to cover a significantly larger area while keeping accurate logs of how long each scanned vehicle was parked in the given location.
Another main feature of the GO-4 Interceptor was their sliding door design. This prevents collisions from bikes or other vehicles which may have otherwise hit the open door - commonly referred to as "Dooring".
Media References
The affordable nature of the GO-4 Interceptor made it an accessible vehicle to be used in many movies and tv shows over the years.
IMCDB lists credits for the GO-4 Interceptor in over 70 different productions.
These often include movies where police vehicles are commonly seen, but the GO-4 Interceptor can be seen in the background of many more films or T.V. shows, though it is often confused with the Cushman Truckster which similarly was awarded early contracts by NYPD for their three wheeled utility vehicles.
The GO-4 Interceptor can also be seen getting a new body to replicate the boat style vehicles from SpongeBob Square Pants by Louis Weisz as well as being created as an available mod to GTA 5 by SteveTheGamer55.
